evidence.explanation: Stroke in 16.9% and non-stroke embolization in 22.6% of a 2781-patient international cohort quantify the systemic embolic burden this node asserts.

steps/8.description: Conformance here needs justifying, because the thrombogenesis module explicitly excludes nonthrombotic emboli. The claim is that a septic vegetation is not a nonthrombotic embolus. It is a fibrin-platelet thrombus with organisms in it, formed by the same platelet and coagulation machinery the module models, and the vascular occlusion and downstream ischaemic injury it causes are thrombotic in exactly the module's sense. The infection changes what is inside the thrombus and adds a septic dimension to the resulting infarct; it does not change the occlusive mechanism. Fragments embolise to brain, spleen, kidneys, and extremities, producing stroke, infarction, mycotic aneurysm, and peripheral lesions. Embolic stroke is both a major cause of morbidity and a complication that constrains surgery, since anticoagulation and cardiopulmonary bypass carry haemorrhagic risk in a recently infarcted brain.

evidence.snippet: Prospective cohort study of 2781 adults with definite IE who were admitted to 58 hospitals in 25 countries from June 1, 2000, through September 1, 2005.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the scale and international scope of the cohort that characterises modern outcomes in this disease.

steps/9.description: The terminal common pathway and the dominant determinant of early mortality, arising from acute regurgitation, myocardial abscess, conduction disturbance, and sepsis together.

steps/10.description: The most common presenting feature, arising from the systemic inflammatory response to persistent high-density infection.

steps/11.description: Reflects valvular regurgitation from leaflet destruction. A new or changing murmur in a febrile patient is the classic combination that should raise the diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: The following complications were common: stroke (16.9%), embolization other than stroke (22.6%), heart failure (32.3%), and intracardiac abscess (14.4%).
evidence.explanation: Gives heart failure at 32.3 percent, which sits in the FREQUENT band of 30 to 79 percent.

steps/12.description: Usually from acute valvular regurgitation, and the dominant predictor of early mortality.

evidence.snippet: The following complications were common: stroke (16.9%), embolization other than stroke (22.6%), heart failure (32.3%), and intracardiac abscess (14.4%).
evidence.explanation: Gives stroke at 16.9 percent, which sits in the OCCASIONAL band of 5 to 29 percent.

steps/13.description: Embolic, from vegetation fragments reaching the cerebral circulation. It is among the most consequential complications because it also complicates the decision to operate.

steps/14.description: A classic finding of subacute disease, reflecting chronic immune stimulation and splenic embolic involvement.

steps/15.description: From renal embolic infarction or from immune complex glomerulonephritis, which are two different mechanisms producing the same finding.

evidence.snippet: The following complications were common: stroke (16.9%), embolization other than stroke (22.6%), heart failure (32.3%), and intracardiac abscess (14.4%).
evidence.explanation: Gives intracardiac abscess at 14.4 percent, in the OCCASIONAL band. The phenotype is bound to a general cardiac morphology term because HPO has no perivalvular abscess concept.

steps/16.description: Perivalvular extension of infection beyond the annulus, which is both a marker of uncontrolled infection and an indication for surgery. It is also a strong independent predictor of death.

steps/17.description: Acute regurgitation from leaflet perforation or chordal rupture, poorly tolerated because the ventricle and atrium have not had time to adapt.

steps/18.description: The aortic equivalent, and the lesion most likely to precipitate rapid decompensation.

edges/0.description: The fibrin-platelet surface provides the binding substrate that circulating organisms require in order to establish infection.

edges/1.description: Circulating organisms must be present at the same time as a receptive surface.

edges/2.description: Adherent organisms proliferate within the fibrin matrix rather than being cleared.

edges/3.description: Ongoing infection at the valve destroys the tissue it sits on.

edges/4.description: The vegetation is friable and fragments detach into the circulation.

edges/5.description: Persistent high-density infection drives a sustained systemic inflammatory response.

edges/6.description: Cytokine release in response to persistent high-density bacteraemia is what produces the fever that is the commonest presenting feature.

edges/7.description: Sustained immune stimulation by a continuously seeding endovascular focus enlarges the spleen, which is the classic subacute finding.

edges/8.description: Circulating immune complexes deposit in glomeruli and produce a glomerulonephritis; this is one of the two mechanisms behind haematuria in this disease, the other being renal embolic infarction.

edges/9.description: Acute valvular incompetence imposes a sudden volume load on an unprepared ventricle.

edges/10.description: Leaflet perforation and chordal rupture of the mitral apparatus produce acute mitral incompetence.

edges/11.description: Destruction of the aortic leaflets produces acute aortic incompetence, the lesion most likely to precipitate rapid decompensation.

edges/12.description: The regurgitant jet across the destroyed valve is audible, so a new or changing murmur in a febrile patient is the classic bedside combination.

edges/13.description: Extension of infection beyond the valve annulus into perivalvular tissue is what an intracardiac abscess is.

edges/14.description: Systemic embolic and septic injury compounds cardiac decompensation.

edges/15.description: Vegetation fragments reaching the cerebral circulation occlude it, producing the embolic stroke that both drives morbidity and constrains the decision to operate.

edges/16.description: Fragments lodging in the renal circulation produce infarction, the embolic half of the two mechanisms that generate haematuria here.

edges/17.description: Haemodynamic decompensation from acute regurgitation, abscess, and sepsis presents clinically as congestive heart failure, the dominant predictor of early mortality.

evidence.snippet: Sixty-two patients were intravenous drug users (IVDU); all but 1 of these had an obvious cutaneous portal of entry related to the injection of illicit drugs.
evidence.explanation: In a prospective bacteraemia series, essentially every injecting patient had a cutaneous portal of entry attributable to injection, which is the route into the bloodstream this edge asserts. The series is of group A streptococcal bacteraemia, so it evidences the route rather than the organism that predominates in endocarditis.

evidence.snippet: Of the remaining 40 evaluable medically treated patients (median age 28, range 20-55), 37 (93%) cultured methicillin-sensitive S. aureus and all had tricuspid valve involvement.
evidence.explanation: Right-sided, skin-flora disease in a young cohort is the signature of organisms entering the venous circulation directly, which is the bacteraemia step this edge asserts.

edges/18.description: Repeated non-sterile injection introduces organisms directly into the bloodstream.

evidence.snippet: With an ageing population and increasing use of implantable cardiac devices and heart valves, the epidemiology of IE has changed.
evidence.explanation: States that device use and population ageing have changed who gets this disease, which is the claim this exposure entry makes.

edges/19.description: Mechanical irritation from intravascular material injures endothelium and provides a non-endothelialised surface on which thrombus forms.

treatments/0.description: Bactericidal antibiotics for four to six weeks, the duration being dictated by the biofilm protection of the vegetation rather than by the organism's intrinsic susceptibility. This is the definitional treatment of the disease and the reason it carries such a burden of hospitalisation.

evidence.snippet: Patients with infective endocarditis on the left side of the heart are typically treated with intravenous antibiotic agents for up to 6 weeks.
evidence.explanation: States the standard of care that this treatment represents, and the duration that the biofilm mechanism accounts for.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Sustained bactericidal exposure is required to sterilise organisms shielded within the fibrin scaffold.

evidence.snippet: In a randomized, noninferiority, multicenter trial, we assigned 400 adults in stable condition who had endocarditis on the left side of the heart caused by streptococcus, Enterococcus faecalis, Staphylococcus aureus, or coagulase-negative staphylococci and who were being treated with intravenous antibiotics to continue intravenous treatment (199 patients) or to switch to oral antibiotic treatment (201 patients).
evidence.explanation: Describes the trial design and its eligibility restrictions, namely stabilised left-sided disease caused by four named organism groups, which is what bounds how far this result generalises.

treatments/1.description: A step-down to oral antibiotics once the patient is stable, tested against continued intravenous therapy in a randomised noninferiority trial. It is curated because it changes the practical shape of the illness rather than its biology, converting weeks of hospitalisation into outpatient treatment for suitable patients. It applies to stabilised left-sided disease caused by specific organisms, not to everyone.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: The antimicrobial target is unchanged; only the route and setting differ.

evidence.snippet: Clinical scenarios in IE are often complex, requiring prompt diagnosis, early institution of antibiotics, and decision-making related to complications, including risk of embolism and timing of surgery when indicated.
evidence.explanation: States the surgical decision problem this treatment sits inside, and names embolic risk and timing as the factors that govern it, which is the judgement the entry describes.

evidence.snippet: The importance of an early, multispecialty team approach to patients with IE is emphasized.
evidence.explanation: Records the guideline emphasis on team-based decision-making, which is the practical answer to a timing question that no single specialty can resolve alone.

treatments/2.description: Excision of infected tissue with valve repair or replacement, indicated for heart failure, uncontrolled infection, abscess, or a high embolic risk. Surgery is curated here as mechanism-directed rather than as rescue, because removing the vegetation removes the protected compartment that antibiotics cannot reliably reach. Timing is genuinely difficult when embolic stroke has already occurred, since bypass and anticoagulation carry haemorrhagic risk in a recently infarcted brain.

evidence.snippet: which has a high virulence rate and a tendency to form a biofilm, meaning that non-surgical therapy may not be effective
evidence.explanation: States that biofilm formation can make medical therapy ineffective, which is the mechanistic rationale for surgery acting where antibiotics cannot.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Excision physically removes the biofilm-protected compartment rather than attempting to penetrate it.

treatments/2/targets/1.description: Repair or replacement restores valve competence after the tissue has been destroyed.

evidence.snippet: Given the logistical challenges of a randomised trial, high-quality case-control studies would help to evaluate the role of dental procedures in causing IE and the efficacy of AP in its prevention.
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL. The authors' own statement that the question remains open and that a randomised trial is impractical, which is why this is likely to stay unresolved.

treatments/3.description: Given to high-risk patients before certain dental procedures on the reasoning that procedural bacteraemia seeds the valve. The evidence for it is weak, and this treatment is curated principally to record that. The mechanistic case is intuitive and the empirical case is not established, and the discrepancy is instructive rather than embarrassing, because everyday bacteraemia from chewing and brushing plausibly dwarfs the procedural contribution.

evidence.snippet: The evidence base for the use of AP is limited, heterogeneous and the methodological quality of many studies is poor. Postprocedural bacteraemia is not a good surrogate endpoint for IE.
evidence.explanation: This link makes a pharmacological claim - that prophylaxis suppresses procedural bacteraemia - and the quoted sentence does not bear on it. What the sentence denies is that reducing bacteraemia predicts reduced IE, which is the bacteraemia-to-endocarditis step rather than the drug-to-bacteraemia one; if anything, using bacteraemia as a surrogate at all presumes the drug lowers it. So NO_EVIDENCE, not REFUTE. The same sentence is cited as SUPPORT in the discussion below, where the claim is that the controversy exists - one quote bearing on two different claims, which is what supports being claim-relative means.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: Prophylaxis aims to suppress procedural bacteraemia before it can seed a receptive surface.

evidence.snippet: The evidence base for the use of AP is limited, heterogeneous and the methodological quality of many studies is poor. Postprocedural bacteraemia is not a good surrogate endpoint for IE.
evidence.explanation: Establishes both that the direct evidence is inadequate and that the surrogate endpoint underpinning the mechanistic case is invalid.

evidence.snippet: Given the logistical challenges of a randomised trial, high-quality case-control studies would help to evaluate the role of dental procedures in causing IE and the efficacy of AP in its prevention.
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL. States why the question is likely to remain open and what design could still address it, which is what makes this a standing controversy rather than a resolved negative.

open_questions/0.rationale: The mechanistic argument is straightforward. Dental procedures cause bacteraemia, bacteraemia seeds a receptive endocardial surface, so suppressing the bacteraemia should prevent the disease. Practice guidelines have progressively narrowed the indication anyway, because the evidence never supported the inference. A systematic review found the evidence base limited and heterogeneous and, more damagingly, concluded that post-procedural bacteraemia is not a good surrogate for the disease, which removes the empirical link the mechanistic argument depends on. The plausible explanation is that cumulative everyday bacteraemia from chewing and tooth brushing dwarfs the procedural contribution, in which case prophylaxis targets a negligible fraction of exposure. This entry curates the practice with its own contradicting evidence attached rather than omitting it, because omission would leave the mechanistic argument looking unopposed. The question is unlikely to be settled, since the authors themselves note that a randomised trial is logistically impractical for so rare an outcome.

evidence.snippet: This shift is of concern as it is associated with Staphylococcus Aureus which has a high virulence rate and a tendency to form a biofilm
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL. The rise of a highly virulent organism able to affect structurally normal valves is what makes the strictness of the thrombus-first requirement an open rather than a settled question.

open_questions/1.rationale: The standard model holds that infection requires a sterile platelet-fibrin thrombus to seed, which explains why bacteraemia is common and this disease is rare, why abnormal valves are the substrate, and why prosthetic material carries such risk. It is also why three nodes of this entry conform to the thrombogenesis module even though the disease is infectious. The model is hard to observe directly in humans, because the sterile lesion is asymptomatic and is found only incidentally or at autopsy, so the requirement is inferred from animal models and from the epidemiology rather than demonstrated prospectively. Two things follow if it is strictly true. Identifying who carries a sterile vegetation would identify who is actually at risk, which is a far better targeting strategy than the current one based on valve category. And Staphylococcus aureus, which can infect apparently normal valves, would need either an unrecognised microscopic thrombus or a genuinely distinct route of invasion, and which of those is correct is not settled.

evidence.snippet: Influenza virus possesses an RNA genome of single-stranded, negative-sensed, and segmented configuration. Influenza virus causes an acute respiratory disease, commonly known as the "flu" in humans. In some individuals, flu can lead to pneumonia and acute respiratory distress syndrome.
evidence.explanation: Describes influenza as an acute respiratory disease caused by viral infection of the respiratory tract.

steps/0.description: Influenza viruses bind to sialic acid residues on respiratory epithelial cells via hemagglutinin, followed by endocytosis and viral replication in the nucleus. Viral neuraminidase facilitates release of new virions. This causes direct cytopathic damage to airway epithelium, leading to desquamation, impaired mucociliary clearance, and susceptibility to secondary bacterial infection.

evidence.snippet: Because TLRs may act as a double-edged sword, a balanced TLR response is critical for the overall benefit of the host.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the dual role of TLR signaling in both antiviral defense and immunopathology during influenza.

evidence.snippet: Host cells sense IAV infection through multiple receptors and mechanisms, which culminate in the induction of a concerted innate antiviral response and the creation of an antiviral state, which inhibits and clears the infection from host cells.
evidence.explanation: Describes innate antiviral sensing mechanisms including TLR pathways.

steps/1.description: Innate immune sensing of influenza occurs through endosomal TLR3, TLR7, and TLR8. TLR7/8 signal via MYD88 to activate IRF5/IRF7 and NF-kappaB, while TLR3 signals via TRIF to activate IRF3 via TBK1/IKK-epsilon. This dual signaling induces type I and III interferons, pro-inflammatory cytokines, and chemokines. The TLR response is a double-edged sword: necessary for viral control but capable of driving immunopathology when hyperactivated.

evidence.snippet: Paradoxically, AIM2 deficiency has been linked to both enhanced and reduced vulnerability to IAV infection.
evidence.explanation: Describes the complex role of AIM2 inflammasome in influenza pathogenesis.

evidence.snippet: While a strong response is necessary for early viral control, overactivation of inflammasomes can precipitate harmful hyperinflammatory responses, a defining characteristic observed during severe influenza infections.
evidence.explanation: Confirms that inflammasome overactivation drives hyperinflammation in severe influenza.

steps/2.description: IAV infection activates NLRP3 and AIM2 inflammasomes. AIM2, canonically a cytosolic dsDNA sensor, is activated by host mitochondrial DNA released after IAV-induced mitochondrial damage. Inflammasome activation leads to caspase-1-mediated processing of IL-1-beta and IL-18, and gasdermin D-mediated pyroptosis. Excessive inflammasome activation contributes to the cytokine storm associated with severe influenza.

evidence.snippet: Influenza A virus (IAV) infection initiates a complex interplay of cell death modalities, including apoptosis, necroptosis, pyroptosis, and their integration, known as PANoptosis, which significantly impacts host immune responses and tissue integrity.
evidence.explanation: Directly describes PANoptosis as integrated cell death modalities in IAV infection.

steps/3.description: Influenza A virus triggers multiple regulated cell death pathways including apoptosis, necroptosis, and pyroptosis, integrated as PANoptosis. ZBP1 senses viral Z-RNA and coordinates these death pathways via RHIM-dependent interactions with RIPK3/RIPK1. MLKL-driven membrane rupture during necroptosis activates NLRP3 inflammasome. Caspase-3 can cleave gasdermin E, linking apoptosis to pyroptosis. This integrated cell death ensures viral clearance but can intensify tissue damage.

evidence.snippet: A total of 854 patients with severe influenza were included in the analysis. The incidence of VTE was 9.37% (80/854).
evidence.explanation: Quantifies VTE incidence in critically ill influenza patients.

steps/4.description: Severe influenza involves pulmonary microvascular endothelial infection and activation, leading to vascular leakage, adhesion molecule upregulation (ICAM-1, VCAM-1), and thromboinflammatory complications including venous thromboembolism. In critically ill influenza cohorts, VTE incidence has been reported at 9.37%.

evidence.snippet: The incidence ratio of an admission for acute myocardial infarction during the risk interval as compared with the control interval was 6.05
evidence.explanation: Self-controlled case-series quantifies a ~6-fold increased risk of acute MI in the first 7 days after laboratory-confirmed influenza, establishing influenza as an acute MI trigger.

evidence.snippet: Acute myocardial infarction can be triggered by acute respiratory infections.
evidence.explanation: States the mechanistic premise that acute respiratory infection, including influenza, can trigger acute myocardial infarction.

steps/5.description: Acute influenza is a recognized short-term trigger of acute myocardial infarction. Influenza-driven systemic inflammation, endothelial activation, platelet activation, and a procoagulant shift can destabilize vulnerable coronary atherosclerotic plaque and precipitate atherothrombotic occlusion, with the excess risk concentrated in the first 7 days after infection. In a self-controlled case-series of laboratory-confirmed influenza, the incidence of hospitalization for acute myocardial infarction was about six-fold higher during the 7-day risk interval than during the control interval, with no increased incidence after day 7. This makes acute MI an important downstream cardiovascular sequela of influenza beyond the respiratory tract, and underpins the cardioprotective rationale for influenza vaccination.

edges/0.description: The acute systemic inflammatory and prothrombotic state of influenza acts as a trigger for acute myocardial infarction in the first week after infection.

evidence.snippet: Antiviral agents that target the influenza virus enzyme neuraminidase have been developed for prophylaxis and therapy.
evidence.explanation: Confirms neuraminidase inhibitors as established influenza antivirals.

evidence.snippet: For seasonal influenza, WHO conditionally recommends treatment within 48 hours of symptom onset with oseltamivir for severe illness, and baloxavir for patients at high risk of progression from non-severe to severe illness.
evidence.explanation: The WHO influenza clinical practice guidelines conditionally recommend oseltamivir for severe illness within 48 hours of onset.

treatments/0.description: Oseltamivir (oral) and zanamivir (inhaled) inhibit viral neuraminidase, preventing release of new virions from infected cells. Most effective when administered within 48 hours of symptom onset.

evidence.snippet: For seasonal influenza, WHO conditionally recommends treatment within 48 hours of symptom onset with oseltamivir for severe illness, and baloxavir for patients at high risk of progression from non-severe to severe illness.
evidence.explanation: The WHO influenza guidelines conditionally recommend baloxavir for patients at high risk of progression from non-severe to severe illness.

treatments/1.description: Baloxavir marboxil inhibits the cap-dependent endonuclease of the influenza polymerase complex, blocking viral mRNA synthesis. Single-dose oral therapy that has shown faster symptom resolution compared to oseltamivir in real-world studies.

evidence.snippet: Influenza vaccines are formulated every year to match the circulating strains, as they evolve antigenically owing to antigenic drift.
evidence.explanation: Describes the rationale for annual influenza vaccination.

treatments/2.description: Seasonal influenza vaccination with inactivated, live-attenuated, recombinant, or cell-based vaccines targeting predicted circulating strains is the primary preventive measure.

treatments/3.description: Antipyretics, hydration, and rest for mild cases. Mechanical ventilation and intensive care for severe respiratory failure.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in the FERMT1 gene (also known as KIND1), encoding the focal adhesion protein kindlin-1, underlie the Kindler syndrome (KS), an autosomal recessive skin disorder with an intriguing progressive phenotype comprising skin blistering, photosensitivity, progressive poikiloderma with extensive skin atrophy, and propensity to skin cancer
evidence.explanation: Confirms FERMT1 mutations cause Kindler syndrome through loss of the focal adhesion protein kindlin-1.

evidence.snippet: Kindler syndrome is caused by genetic defects in the focal contact-associated protein, fermitin family homologue 1 (FFH1), encoded by the gene FERMT1 (known as KIND1)
evidence.explanation: Confirms FERMT1 encodes the focal contact-associated protein FFH1 (kindlin-1) and its defects cause Kindler syndrome.

steps/1.description: Loss-of-function mutations in FERMT1 (also known as KIND1) lead to absence or dysfunction of the focal adhesion protein kindlin-1 (fermitin family homolog-1). Most mutations are predicted to lead to premature termination of translation and complete loss of kindlin-1 function, though missense mutations can cause milder phenotypes.

evidence.snippet: active beta1 integrin was reduced but overexpression of fermitin family homolog-1 restored integrin activation and partially rescued the Kindler syndrome cellular phenotype
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that kindlin-1 deficiency reduces active beta1 integrin and that restoring kindlin-1 rescues integrin activation.

evidence.snippet: We identified altered distribution of several basement membrane proteins, including types IV, VII, and XVII collagens and laminin-332 in Kindler syndrome skin
evidence.explanation: Shows disruption of multiple basement membrane components beyond focal adhesions in Kindler syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Defects in FFH1 lead to abnormal integrin activation and loss of keratinocyte epidermal adhesion to the underlying basal lamina, disruption in normal cell cytoskeleton within keratinocytes, and altered signaling pathways
evidence.explanation: Confirms that kindlin-1 deficiency causes abnormal integrin activation and loss of keratinocyte adhesion.

steps/2.description: Kindlin-1 is a FERM domain protein that activates integrin beta1 signaling at the basal keratinocyte-basement membrane zone interface. Loss of kindlin-1 results in reduced active beta1 integrin, altered distribution of basement membrane proteins (types IV, VII, and XVII collagens, laminin-332), and disruption of hemidesmosomal components. This causes impaired cell-ECM adhesion at multiple levels, explaining the mixed-level cleavage characteristic of Kindler EB.

evidence.snippet: lack of this protein leads to pathological changes beyond focal adhesions, with disruption of several hemidesmosomal components and reduced expression of keratinocyte stem cell markers
evidence.explanation: Shows that kindlin-1 loss impairs keratinocyte biology beyond adhesion, including stem cell marker expression, which contributes to impaired wound healing.

steps/3.description: Defective integrin activation and cell-matrix adhesion impair keratinocyte migration and proliferation, leading to poor wound healing. Loss of kindlin-1 also disrupts cytoskeletal organization within keratinocytes and reduces keratinocyte stem cell markers such as cytokeratin 15.

evidence.snippet: an autosomal recessive skin disorder with an intriguing progressive phenotype comprising skin blistering, photosensitivity, progressive poikiloderma with extensive skin atrophy, and propensity to skin cancer
evidence.explanation: Confirms the progressive nature of poikiloderma and skin atrophy in Kindler syndrome.

evidence.snippet: deleting Kindlin-1 in mice gives rise to skin atrophy
evidence.explanation: Mouse model confirms that kindlin-1 loss directly causes skin atrophy.

steps/4.description: Progressive poikiloderma (atrophy, telangiectasia, pigmentary changes) is the hallmark feature of Kindler EB. The mechanism involves chronic defective keratinocyte adhesion leading to cumulative skin damage. Photosensitivity may contribute through oxidative stress in kindlin-1-deficient keratinocytes. Skin atrophy is diffuse and progressive, affecting both sun-exposed and non-exposed areas.

evidence.snippet: deleting Kindlin-1 in mice gives rise to skin atrophy and an intestinal epithelial dysfunction with similarities to human UC
evidence.explanation: Mouse model demonstrates that kindlin-1 loss causes intestinal epithelial dysfunction resembling ulcerative colitis.

evidence.snippet: This intestinal dysfunction results in perinatal lethality and is triggered by defective intestinal epithelial cell integrin activation, leading to detachment of this barrier followed by a destructive inflammatory response
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that intestinal involvement is caused by defective integrin activation in epithelial cells.

evidence.snippet: Mucosal manifestations are also common and include hemorrhagic mucositis and gingivitis, periodontal disease, premature loss of teeth, and labial leukokeratosis. Other mucosal findings can include ectropion, urethral stenosis, and severe phimosis
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews confirms the spectrum of mucosal manifestations in Kindler syndrome.

steps/5.description: Kindler EB affects mucosal epithelium, causing colitis resembling ulcerative colitis, esophageal strictures, urethral stenosis, and oral mucosal fragility with hemorrhagic gingivitis and periodontitis. Mucosal manifestations result from the same integrin activation defect in epithelial cells lining these structures.

edges/1.description: Loss of kindlin-1 disrupts focal adhesion formation and integrin activation at the basal keratinocyte-basement membrane zone interface.

edges/2.description: Defective integrin activation impairs keratinocyte migration and proliferation, leading to delayed wound healing.

edges/3.description: Chronic adhesion defects lead to progressive skin atrophy, telangiectasia, and pigmentary changes (poikiloderma).

evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of KS is established in a proband with suggestive clinical findings and biallelic pathogenic variants in FERMT1 identified by molecular genetic testing
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews confirms biallelic FERMT1 variants as the molecular basis of Kindler syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Although most mutations are predicted to lead to premature termination of translation, and to loss of kindlin-1 function, significant clinical variability is observed among patients
evidence.explanation: Confirms that most FERMT1 mutations are loss-of-function with variable clinical expression.

evidence.snippet: It results from loss-of-function mutations in the FERMT1 gene encoding the focal adhesion protein, fermitin family homolog-1
evidence.explanation: Confirms FERMT1 loss-of-function mutations cause Kindler syndrome.

genes/0.notes: FERMT1 (also known as KIND1) encodes kindlin-1 (fermitin family homolog-1), a focal adhesion protein that activates integrins. Located on chromosome 20p12.3. Mutations include gross genomic deletions, splice site, nonsense, frameshift, and missense mutations. Missense and in-frame deletion mutations are associated with milder phenotypes and later onset of complications.

evidence.snippet: Skin care includes standard blister care, use of moisturizers, and protection from trauma and the sun
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews describes wound care and skin protection as key management strategies.

treatments/0.description: Standard blister care with use of moisturizers and protection from mechanical trauma. Multidisciplinary management by a team experienced in skin fragility disorders is recommended.

evidence.snippet: Agents/circumstances to avoid: Sun exposure
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews explicitly recommends avoiding sun exposure.

treatments/1.description: Sun avoidance and sunscreen use to reduce photosensitivity-related skin damage. Sun exposure is listed as an agent to avoid.

evidence.snippet: management of gastrointestinal and urethral complications
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews includes GI management as part of treatment.

treatments/2.description: Management of gastrointestinal complications including colitis and esophageal strictures. Gastroenterology input is part of the multidisciplinary team.

evidence.snippet: regular dental care to ensure optimal oral hygiene to reduce periodontal disease
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews recommends regular dental care for periodontal disease prevention.

treatments/3.description: Regular dental care to ensure optimal oral hygiene and reduce periodontal disease. Screening for oral ulcerations, gingivitis, and periodontitis starting in adolescence with regular dental checkups.

evidence.snippet: Screening for premalignant keratoses and early squamous cell carcinomas starting in adolescence and repeated annually
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews recommends annual SCC screening starting in adolescence.

treatments/4.description: Screening for premalignant keratoses and early squamous cell carcinomas starting in adolescence and repeated annually.

evidence.snippet: KS is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner. If both parents are known to be heterozygous for an FERMT1 pathogenic variant, each sib of an affected individual has at conception a 25% chance of being affected
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews confirms autosomal recessive inheritance and recommends genetic counseling.

treatments/5.description: Kindler syndrome is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner. Carrier testing for at-risk relatives, prenatal testing, and preimplantation genetic testing are possible once FERMT1 pathogenic variants have been identified.

evidence.snippet: loss of Kindlin-1 in mouse keratinocytes recapitulates Kindler syndrome and also produces enlarged and hyperactive stem cell compartments, which lead to hyperthickened epidermis, ectopic hair follicle development and increased skin tumor susceptibility
evidence.explanation: Mouse model demonstrates that kindlin-1 loss leads to stem cell hyperactivation and tumor susceptibility through Wnt pathway dysregulation.

evidence.snippet: loss of Kindlin-1 induces nuclear translocation of β-catenin-Lef1 in KS and mouse skin leading to elevated Wnt-β-catenin signaling
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates the specific mechanism of nuclear beta-catenin-Lef1 translocation in both mouse model and human KS skin.

evidence.snippet: Kindlin-1 controls keratinocyte adhesion through β1-class integrins and proliferation and differentiation of cutaneous epithelial stem cells by promoting α(v)β(6) integrin-mediated transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) activation and inhibiting Wnt-β-catenin signaling through integrin-independent regulation of Wnt ligand expression
evidence.explanation: Defines the dual mechanism by which kindlin-1 normally suppresses tumorigenesis through TGF-beta activation and Wnt inhibition.

evidence.snippet: autocrine TGF-beta 1 suppresses the frequency and rate of malignant progression
evidence.explanation: Independent validation of the TGF-β arm of the canonical model: keratinocyte-specific TGF-β1 deletion produces rapid SCC progression, directly testing the tumor-suppressive role of TGF-β signaling that kindlin-1 loss disrupts.

evidence.snippet: enhanced Smad3/Smad4-mediated Snail transcription contributed to Smad2 loss-associated EMT during skin carcinogenesis
evidence.explanation: Keratinocyte-specific Smad2 ablation accelerates SCC formation with EMT and Snail upregulation, independently validating that loss of TGF-β/Smad signaling is sufficient to accelerate skin carcinogenesis — supporting the TGF-β arm of the canonical model.

evidence.snippet: development of a hypoxic tumor environment and increased glycolysis
evidence.explanation: Qualifies the canonical model: kindlin-1 loss in SCC also drives tumor progression through a hypoxic/MMP13-mediated invasion pathway independent of the Wnt-driven stem-cell expansion mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Kindlin-1 deletion led to profound suppression of gene expression of the antioxidant enzyme Gstp1 and exacerbated ultraviolet radiation (UVR) induced DNA damage
evidence.explanation: Qualifies the canonical model: kindlin-1 loss also drives EMT/fibrosis and suppresses Gstp1 antioxidant defense, providing a tumor-permissive microenvironment via UV-damage accumulation that operates in parallel with the Wnt arm.

evidence.snippet: concentrated in the hands and around the oral cavity, which are areas of high inflammation in this disease
evidence.explanation: Largest clinical KS cohort (n=91) shows SCC body distribution concentrated at chronic-inflammation sites with 66.7% cumulative risk by age >60 and 53.8% metastatic rate, consistent with a multi-hit pathogenesis layered on the canonical model.

hypotheses/0.description: Loss of kindlin-1 induces nuclear translocation of beta-catenin-Lef1 in keratinocytes, leading to elevated Wnt-beta-catenin signaling. This dysregulation produces enlarged and hyperactive cutaneous epithelial stem cell compartments, resulting in hyperthickened epidermis, ectopic hair follicle development, and increased skin tumor susceptibility. Kindlin-1 normally inhibits Wnt-beta-catenin signaling through integrin-independent regulation of Wnt ligand expression, and simultaneously promotes TGF-beta-mediated growth-inhibitory signals via alphav-beta6 integrin. Loss of this dual control shifts the balance toward unchecked proliferation.

evidence.snippet: loss of Kindlin-1 sensitizes both SCC cells and keratinocytes to oxidative stress: Kindlin-1 deficient cells have higher levels of reactive oxygen species, decreased viability and increased DNA damage after treatment with either hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) or irradiation with UVA
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that kindlin-1-deficient cells have elevated ROS and increased susceptibility to oxidative DNA damage.

evidence.snippet: Kindlin-1 is required to fully activate ERK signalling after oxidative damage, and that activation of ERK protects cells from DNA damage following oxidative stress
evidence.explanation: Identifies impaired ERK signaling as the molecular mechanism linking kindlin-1 loss to oxidative stress vulnerability.

evidence.snippet: Kindlin-1 dependent activation of ERK signalling is a key molecular mechanism that renders KS keratinocytes more sensitive to oxidative damage and contributes to the increased photosensitivity in KS patients
evidence.explanation: Directly proposes this mechanism as the basis for photosensitivity in Kindler syndrome patients.

evidence.snippet: the Kindlin-1 dependent activation of ERK and protection from DNA damage following oxidative stress depends on the ability of Kindlin-1 to bind integrins
evidence.explanation: Substantiates the "integrin-dependent" wording of this hypothesis: the ERK activation and the DNA-damage protection it confers were both shown to require kindlin-1's integrin-binding ability. Integrin dependence is therefore a tested result here, not an assumption carried over from kindlin-1's canonical adhesion role, and kindlin-1's other integrin-independent activities do not bear on it.

evidence.snippet: These cytokines are dependent on p38 activation
evidence.explanation: Qualifies the ERK-specific arm: independent KS-keratinocyte data show p38-dependent (not ERK-dependent) pro-inflammatory cytokine upregulation in response to UV-B, and antioxidant rescue confirms the ROS-driven photosensitivity phenotype broadly.

evidence.snippet: KIND1 loss impaired DNA repair, as indicated by the increased
evidence.explanation: Qualifies the canonical ERK-centric model: KIND1 loss activates NF-κB and JNK inflammatory signaling pathways, drives CPD/γH2AX accumulation post-UVB, and JNK/NF-κB inhibition restores DNA repair — implicating multi-pathway signaling deficiency rather than ERK alone.

evidence.snippet: UV-B irradiation induced loss of kindlin-2 in keratinocytes
evidence.explanation: Adds a "double-hit" qualification: UV-B exposure depletes the compensatory kindlin-2 paralog, worsening kindlin-1-deficient keratinocyte function and amplifying the photosensitivity phenotype.

evidence.snippet: kindlin-1 can associate directly with EGFR in vitro and in keratinocytes in an EGF-dependent, integrin-independent manner
evidence.explanation: Qualifies the "integrin-dependent" framing of the canonical model: kindlin-1 directly stabilizes EGFR in an integrin-independent manner. Kindlin-1 loss reduces EGFR levels, which may also contribute to photosensitivity through impaired survival/proliferative signaling.

hypotheses/1.description: Kindlin-1-deficient keratinocytes have higher baseline levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and show decreased viability and increased DNA damage after oxidative stress (H2O2 or UVA irradiation). Kindlin-1 is required for full activation of ERK signaling after oxidative damage, and ERK activation protects cells from DNA damage. This integrin-dependent mechanism explains the photosensitivity characteristic of Kindler syndrome and may contribute to the predisposition to aggressive squamous cell carcinoma through accumulation of UV-induced DNA damage.

evidence.snippet: antioxidants and the plant flavonoid luteolin represent feasible topical therapeutic approaches decreasing UV-B induced apoptosis in two-dimensional and organotypic KS cultures
evidence.explanation: Establishes the untested therapeutic lead this gap turns on — a topical intervention that works on the proposed mechanism in organotypic Kindler cultures and has never been evaluated in patients.

open_questions/0.rationale: Every measurement behind this hypothesis was made in cultured cells. Emmert (PMID:28501563) is the only study that assayed ERK at all, and the two studies usually cited against it did not: the p38 work (PMID:27798104) measured cytokine induction and the NF-κB/JNK work (PMID:27725201) measured DNA-repair readouts, so neither shows ERK is uninvolved or subordinate. What is missing is the comparison — ERK, p38, JNK and NF-κB assayed side by side after matched UVA and UVB doses, which matters because the ERK evidence comes from UVA and the competing evidence from UVB, two wavelengths with different primary mechanisms of damage. Nothing has been measured in patient tissue: no ROS, 8-OHdG, γH2AX or phospho-MAPK study of UV-exposed Kindler skin has been published. The gap is not academic, because the one therapeutic lead the mechanism has produced — topical antioxidants and luteolin, which reduce UV-B apoptosis in organotypic KS cultures (PMID:27798104) — has never been taken into a patient. The completed EB trial curated in this entry (NCT04908215) tested topical cannabinol for wound healing and does not address it.

evidence.snippet: elevation of FERMT1 expression is increased in actinic keratoses compared to normal skin, with a further increase in cSCC supporting a pro-tumorigenic role in this population
evidence.explanation: Documents the opposite-direction half of the paradox in human lesion tissue — FERMT1 rising with progression in sporadic disease — against which the loss-of-function mechanism in Kindler syndrome has to be reconciled.

open_questions/1.rationale: A single study reports both halves, so this is not a discrepancy between laboratories that can be argued away on methodology. Carrasco et al. (PMID:38982038) found FERMT1 expression rising from normal skin to actinic keratosis to cutaneous SCC in non-Kindler patients, consistent with a pro-tumorigenic role, and in the same paper found that depleting kindlin-1 increased SCC growth in vivo and in spheroids through a hypoxic, MMP13-driven route. Kindlin-1 therefore cannot be a simple tumour suppressor whose loss is oncogenic, and the direction of its effect appears to depend on cell state or tumour stage. This matters for how the Wnt/β-catenin model is read: if the relevant variable is context rather than dose, then a mechanism calibrated on germline null keratinocytes may not describe the sporadic disease at all, and any therapeutic inference drawn from one setting does not transfer to the other.

evidence.snippet: we found increased TGFβ signaling and activation of dermal fibroblasts in Kindlin-1 deleted skin, highlighting the importance of paracrine signaling in the control of skin homeostasis by Kindlin-1
evidence.explanation: States the increased-TGF-β observation that sits in tension with the canonical model's loss-of-TGF-β-activation arm, and attributes it to paracrine signalling, which is the reconciliation this discussion proposes to test.

open_questions/2.rationale: The canonical model has kindlin-1 promoting αvβ6-integrin-mediated TGF-β activation, so that its loss removes a growth-inhibitory signal. Carrasco et al. (PMID:42091340) deleted Kindlin-1 in adult mouse epidermis and found increased TGF-β signalling with activation of dermal fibroblasts, a fibrotic matrix and suppressed Gstp1. Both cannot be the same claim about the same signal. The most likely reconciliation is compartmental — autocrine keratinocyte growth inhibition lost, paracrine keratinocyte-to-fibroblast signalling gained — and if that is right the entry should say which arm each piece of evidence speaks to, because a reader currently sees TGF-β cited in both directions in the same hypothesis block. The alternative, that the direction differs between germline and adult-induced deletion, would be a genuine limit on the mouse evidence rather than a labelling problem.

evidence.snippet: the PDGFRB mutations previously identified in familial IM and overgrowth syndrome activate the receptor in the absence of ligand, supporting the hypothesis that these mutations cause the diseases.
evidence.explanation: Confirms constitutive PDGFRB activation underlies the disease.

steps/1.description: Activating PDGFRB mutations cause ligand-independent constitutive receptor signaling.

evidence.snippet: Increased STAT5 phosphorylation and overexpression of Igf1 and Socs2 in PDGFRβD849V cells suggests that overgrowth in mice involves PDGFRβD849V activating the STAT5-IGF1 axis locally in the skeleton.
evidence.explanation: Mouse model demonstrates the STAT5-IGF1 mechanism underlying skeletal overgrowth.

steps/2.description: Mutant PDGFRβ causes increased STAT5 phosphorylation and overexpression of IGF1, activating the STAT5-IGF1 axis locally in the skeleton.

evidence.snippet: Autosomal dominant PDGFRβ gain-of-function mutations in mice and humans cause a spectrum of wasting and overgrowth disorders afflicting the skeleton and other connective tissues
evidence.explanation: Establishes the skeletal overgrowth phenotype from PDGFRB gain-of-function.

evidence.snippet: Mutant cells undergo poor osteogenesis in vitro with increased expression of Sox9 and other chondrogenic markers.
evidence.explanation: In vitro, PDGFRB-mutant skeletal stem cells shift away from osteogenesis toward SOX9-driven chondrogenesis, the cellular basis of skeletal overgrowth.

steps/3.description: Skeletal stem cells from mutant mice show alterations in osteogenic and chondrogenic precursors with promotion of chondrogenesis over osteogenesis, leading to the overgrowth phenotype.

edges/1.description: Constitutive PDGFRB signaling activates the STAT5-IGF1 axis.

edges/2.description: STAT5-IGF1 signaling alters skeletal stem cell fate, promoting chondrogenesis.

evidence.snippet: the germline mutant identified in overgrowth syndrome, P584R, was a stronger oncogene than the germline R561C mutant associated with myofibromatosis.
evidence.explanation: Functional characterization shows P584R is a potent activating variant.

evidence.snippet: Heterozygous activating missense variants of PDGFRB are associated with the phenotype of Kosaki overgrowth syndrome (KOGS).
evidence.explanation: Confirms activating PDGFRB variants cause KOGS.

evidence.snippet: The two known types of pathogenic variants (p.(Pro584Arg) and p.(Trp566Arg)) of the PDGFRB that cause KOGS are exclusively located in the juxtaglomerular domain that regulates autoactivation/inhibition of PDGFRB.
evidence.explanation: Both recurrent KOGS variants map to the juxtamembrane autoinhibitory region of PDGFRB that normally restrains receptor autoactivation ("juxtaglomerular domain" as termed in the source).

evidence.snippet: Importantly, all activated mutants were sensitive to tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as imatinib, nilotinib and ponatinib.
evidence.explanation: In vitro evidence of sensitivity to imatinib.

evidence.snippet: Three patients were treated with imatinib and had robust and rapid response
evidence.explanation: Clinical evidence of imatinib efficacy in PDGFRB spectrum disorders.

evidence.snippet: To prevent the progression of artery dilation, preventative and therapeutic medical measures using tyrosine kinase inhibitors may be necessary in addition to optimal control of the systemic blood pressure.
evidence.explanation: Serial-imaging follow-up of the original KOGS patients proposes tyrosine kinase inhibition to slow progressive arterial dilation.

treatments/0.description: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor that targets constitutively activated PDGFRB. Preclinical data and case reports support its use in PDGFRB gain-of-function disorders.

evidence.snippet: Patients' cells as well as recombinant mutant protein showed reduced glucuronyltransferase activity.
evidence.explanation: Directly demonstrates reduced GlcAT-I catalytic activity as the proximal molecular defect.

evidence.snippet: Further studies demonstrated that GlcAT-I resides in the cis and cis-medial Golgi apparatus and is expressed in the affected tissues, i.e., heart, aorta, and bone.
evidence.explanation: Localizes the enzyme to the cis/cis-medial Golgi and shows expression in the tissues that are clinically affected.

evidence.snippet: the more severe phenotypes appear to harbor mutations located within the acceptor substrate binding subdomain of the catalytic domain of the protein, whereas more mildly affected patients seem to have mutations in the donor substrate binding subdomain
evidence.explanation: Supports the subdomain-based genotype-phenotype correlation described for this node.

steps/1.description: Biallelic B3GAT3 missense, start-loss, or in-frame deletion variants reduce or abolish the galactosylgalactosylxylosylprotein 3-beta-glucuronosyltransferase activity of GlcAT-I. Disease-associated substitutions cluster in the two functional halves of the catalytic domain: the donor (UDP-GlcA) substrate-binding subdomain (p.Pro140Leu, p.Thr139Met, p.Arg161Trp) and the acceptor substrate-binding subdomain (p.Arg277Gln, p.Gly223Ser, p.Leu224Gln, p.Arg297Trp). Reduced activity is demonstrable both in patient-derived cells and for recombinant mutant protein.

evidence.snippet: Linkeropathies are due to enzymatic defects in the synthesis of the common linker region that joins the core proteins to their glycosaminoglycan (GAG) side chains.
evidence.explanation: Defines the shared-linker bottleneck that this node represents.

evidence.snippet: The linker region is completed by the transfer of glucuronic acid (GlcA) catalyzed by glucuronosyltransferase I (GlcAT-I encoded by B3GAT3), upon which polymerization of the HS or CS/DS chains begins.
evidence.explanation: States that GlcAT-I completes the linker and that HS and CS/DS polymerization is downstream of it.

steps/2.description: All glycosaminoglycan chains — heparan sulfate and chondroitin/dermatan sulfate alike — are built on a single shared GlcA-Gal-Gal-Xyl tetrasaccharide linker attached to a serine of the proteoglycan core protein. GlcAT-I catalyzes the final, committing step of linker assembly, so its deficiency is a bottleneck upstream of every downstream GAG polymerase and sulfotransferase. This shared-bottleneck position is what defines the "linkeropathy" disease class and explains why one enzyme defect produces a pleiotropic connective tissue phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Patient fibroblasts demonstrated decreased levels of dermatan sulfate, chondroitin sulfate, and heparan sulfate proteoglycans, indicating that the defect in linker synthesis affected all three lines of O-glycanated proteoglycans.
evidence.explanation: Direct patient-cell measurement of the combined DS/CS/HS proteoglycan deficiency.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, relative numbers of glycosaminoglycan (GAG) side chains were decreased in patient cells.
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation of reduced GAG side-chain occupancy in patient cells.

evidence.snippet: In uxs1 and b3gat3 mutant larvae, biosynthesis of CS was shown to be virtually abolished, whereas these mutants still were capable of synthesizing 50% of the HS produced in control larvae.
evidence.explanation: Zebrafish b3gat3 mutants show a markedly asymmetric CS-versus-HS deficit, qualifying (rather than simply confirming) the balanced reduction inferred from human fibroblasts.

steps/3.description: Patient fibroblasts and lymphoblastoid cells carry reduced numbers of GAG side chains and reduced levels of heparan sulfate, chondroitin sulfate, and dermatan sulfate proteoglycans. Proteoglycans are not only structural space-filling ECM components but also co-receptors and morphogen reservoirs (FGF, BMP, Wnt, Hedgehog), so their simultaneous depletion degrades both the mechanical and the signalling functions of the matrix. The b3gat3 zebrafish mutant qualifies this picture: there, CS synthesis is virtually abolished while roughly half of normal HS output is retained, implying the two arms may not be equally sensitive to loss of the shared linker step.

evidence.snippet: Proteoglycans are a major component of extracellular matrix and contribute to normal embryonic and postnatal development by ensuring tissue stability and signaling functions.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the dual structural and signalling role of the proteoglycan-bearing matrix that is lost here.

steps/4.description: The proteoglycan-poor matrix is mechanically weaker and signals abnormally in the tissues where B3GAT3 is most highly expressed — cartilage, bone, tendon, skeletal muscle, heart and aorta. This is the convergence point from which the three principal clinical arms of the disease diverge: skeletal, articular, and cardiovascular.

evidence.snippet: We identified a novel B3GAT3-related disorder with craniosynostosis and bone fragility, due to a unique homozygous mutation in B3GAT3.
evidence.explanation: Establishes craniosynostosis and bone fragility as part of the severe end of the skeletal arm.

evidence.snippet: a 4-year-old patient with a severe phenotype of osteoporosis, hypotonia, joint laxity, fractures, scoliosis, biscuspid aortic valve and myopia
evidence.explanation: Documents osteoporosis, fractures and scoliosis in a functionally validated B3GAT3 patient.

steps/5.description: Chondrocyte and osteoblast function in a proteoglycan-poor matrix yields disproportionate short stature, metaphyseal flaring and epiphyseal dysplasia, radioulnar synostosis, kyphoscoliosis, and reduced bone mineral density that in severely affected individuals progresses to generalized osteoporosis with multiple fractures. In the most severe (acceptor-subdomain) genotypes the cranial sutures fuse prematurely, producing craniosynostosis and an Antley-Bixler-like prenatal presentation.

evidence.snippet: We studied five patients with recessive joint dislocations and congenital heart defects, including bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and aortic root dilatation.
evidence.explanation: The founding cohort was ascertained on recessive joint dislocations, anchoring this node clinically.

evidence.snippet: While joint hypermobility is a common trait of all LKs, joint contractures are more frequently observed in patients with B3GAT3 and B3GALT6 mutations.
evidence.explanation: Supports the coexistence of hypermobility with contractures and its relative specificity for B3GAT3.

steps/6.description: Ligaments, joint capsules and tendons depend on proteoglycan-rich matrix for tensile integrity. Their weakening produces the cardinal congenital large-joint dislocations (hips, elbows, knees) and generalized joint hypermobility, while the same abnormal periarticular tissue also gives rise to fixed joint contractures — an unusual coexistence of laxity and contracture that is characteristic of B3GAT3 (and B3GALT6) disease among the linkeropathies.

evidence.snippet: The described family constitutes a syndrome characterized by heart defects and joint dislocations resulting from altered initiation of proteoglycan synthesis (Larsen-like syndrome, B3GAT3 type).
evidence.explanation: Attributes the cardiac defects directly to altered initiation of proteoglycan synthesis, and names the disease entity.

evidence.snippet: no heart phenotype could be detected in our family.

steps/7.description: Proteoglycan-rich cardiac jelly and valve interstitial matrix are required for endocardial cushion remodelling and semilunar/atrioventricular valve morphogenesis, and proteoglycans are structural constituents of the aortic media. GlcAT-I deficiency therefore yields bicuspid aortic valve, mitral valve prolapse, atrial and ventricular septal defects, and progressive aortic root dilatation. Cardiovascular involvement is the feature that most sharply distinguishes B3GAT3-related disease from the B4GALT7/B3GALT6 spondylodysplastic Ehlers-Danlos linkeropathies, and it is genotype-dependent: the Nias p.Pro140Leu donor-subdomain family had no detectable cardiac phenotype.

evidence.snippet: We studied five patients with recessive joint dislocations and congenital heart defects, including bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and aortic root dilatation.

evidence.snippet: The phenotypic features with a high rate of incidence shared among all LKs include short stature, joint laxity with dislocations, craniofacial dysmorphism (especially prominent forehead/eyes and blue sclerae), pectus abnormalities, peculiar fingers, foot deformities, and to a variable degree hypotonia and developmental delay.

evidence.snippet: We report on a patient with a novel homozygous B3GAT3 (c.667G>A, p.Gly223Ser) mutation and a history of multiple fractures, blue sclerae, and glaucoma.
evidence.explanation: Documents blue sclerae.

evidence.snippet: The patient also showed skin hyperextensibility over the neck, elbow, forearm and knees, easy bruising, mild atrophic scarring, generalized joint hypermobility with a Beighton score (BS) of 6/9, clinodactyly of the fifth finger, and long fingers with spatulate distal phalanges.

steps/27.description: Cutaneous involvement is variable and likely under-ascertained because most reports focused on skeletal features: skin hyperextensibility over the neck, elbows, forearms and knees with easy bruising and mild atrophic scarring in the compound heterozygous adolescent; excessive palmar and plantar skin wrinkling with normal elasticity in a p.Arg277Gln homozygote; and cutis laxa in the severe p.Gly223Ser neonate and the geroderma osteodysplastica-like p.Pro82Leu case. These findings are grouped under their shared HPO parent; wrinkling and cutis laxa are not evidence of hyperextensibility itself. The 2014 report described hyperextensibility as absent in the six patients then known, whereas later cases document it. A frequency band is not assigned because cutaneous ascertainment was incomplete.

evidence.snippet: hypermobility, severe kyphoscoliosis, osteoporosis with multiple fractures in childhood, congenital diaphragmatic hernia, minor dental anomalies, digital malformations, and characteristic facial features.

evidence.snippet: We found that Pro140Leu-mutant GlcAT-I cannot efficiently transfer GlcA to the linker region trisaccharide.
evidence.explanation: Shows directly that the mutant enzyme fails to complete the linker tetrasaccharide.

edges/1.description: Loss of the terminal glucuronosyl transfer step leaves the linker trisaccharide unfinished, so glycosaminoglycan polymerization cannot begin.

evidence.snippet: This failure results in a partial deficiency of both chondroitin sulfate and heparan sulfate chains.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates the combined, non-selective GAG deficiency.

edges/2.description: Because the blocked step is shared, both the heparan sulfate and the chondroitin/dermatan sulfate arms of proteoglycan synthesis are reduced together rather than one selectively.

evidence.snippet: As a major component of the extracellular matrix, proteoglycans influence the mechanical properties of connective tissue and play an important role in cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions.
evidence.explanation: Links proteoglycan loss to altered mechanical and adhesive properties of connective tissue matrix.

evidence.explanation: Establishes the causal step from GAG deficiency to failure of pericellular extracellular matrix formation around chondrocytes.

edges/3.description: Loss of GAG-bearing proteoglycans changes the composition and mechanical behaviour of the extracellular matrix in connective tissue.

evidence.snippet: The study shows that reduced GlcAT-I activity impairs skeletal as well as heart development
evidence.explanation: States that reduced GlcAT-I activity impairs skeletal development.

edges/4.description: Cartilage and bone matrix depend heavily on proteoglycan content, so the matrix defect manifests as disproportionate short stature, metaphyseal and epiphyseal dysplasia, radioulnar synostosis and low bone mineral density.

evidence.snippet: Linkeropathies are a group of syndromes characterized by short stature, radio-ulnar synostosis, decreased bone density, congenital contractures and dislocations, joint laxity, broad digits, brachycephaly, small mouth, prominent eyes, short or webbed neck, congenital heart defects and mild developmental delay.

edges/5.description: Weakened, proteoglycan-poor periarticular connective tissue permits congenital and recurrent large-joint dislocation and, paradoxically, joint contracture.

evidence.snippet: The study shows that reduced GlcAT-I activity impairs skeletal as well as heart development and results in variable combinations of heart malformations, including mitral valve prolapse, ventricular septal defect, and bicuspid aortic valve.
evidence.explanation: Directly links the enzyme defect to the spectrum of cardiac malformations.

edges/6.description: Cardiac cushion and valve morphogenesis and aortic wall assembly are proteoglycan-dependent; B3GAT3 is expressed in heart and aorta and is relatively more highly expressed in heart than the other linker enzymes, which is the leading explanation for why cardiac malformation is the distinguishing feature of this linkeropathy.

evidence.snippet: This is a group of multisystem conditions characterized by different phenotypes that include skeletal dysplasia and various extra-skeletal features: developmental delay/intellectual disability, ophthalmological abnormalities including blue sclerae, facial characteristics, cardiac defects, abdominal wall defects (hernias), cutis laxa, hypermobility and hypotonia.

edges/7.description: Thin, proteoglycan-poor scleral connective tissue letting the underlying uveal pigment show through is the presumed mechanism, by analogy with osteogenesis imperfecta; scleral thinning itself has not been measured in this disorder.

evidence.snippet: This is a group of multisystem conditions characterized by different phenotypes that include skeletal dysplasia and various extra-skeletal features: developmental delay/intellectual disability, ophthalmological abnormalities including blue sclerae, facial characteristics, cardiac defects, abdominal wall defects (hernias), cutis laxa, hypermobility and hypotonia.
evidence.explanation: Attributes hernias to the linkeropathy connective tissue defect at the disease level; the quoted hernias are abdominal wall defects — diaphragmatic herniation is placed in the same connective-tissue class by inference, not by the quoted text.

edges/8.description: Generalized connective tissue weakness predisposes to diaphragmatic and abdominal wall hernias; the diaphragm-specific developmental step has not been characterized in this disorder.

evidence.snippet: This is a group of multisystem conditions characterized by different phenotypes that include skeletal dysplasia and various extra-skeletal features: developmental delay/intellectual disability, ophthalmological abnormalities including blue sclerae, facial characteristics, cardiac defects, abdominal wall defects (hernias), cutis laxa, hypermobility and hypotonia.
evidence.explanation: Attributes cutis laxa and cutaneous involvement to the linkeropathy connective tissue defect at the disease-group level; the dermal intermediate — proteoglycan-depleted fibroblast matrix — is separately measured in patient cells (PMID:21763480), which is why the link is typed with known intermediates.

edges/10.description: Impaired endochondral growth of the proteoglycan-poor cartilage template manifests as the near-universal disproportionate short stature.

evidence.snippet: Radioulnar synostosis seems more specific for B3GAT3-and B4GALT7-related disorders

edges/11.description: Aberrant forearm skeletal morphogenesis produces the hallmark bilateral proximal radioulnar synostosis with dysplastic radial heads.

edges/12.description: Deficient mineral accrual in the proteoglycan-poor bone matrix presents as osteopenia progressing to generalized osteoporosis.

edges/13.description: The same low-mineral-density, matrix-deficient bone is mechanically fragile; severe (acceptor-subdomain) genotypes fracture repeatedly, sometimes from the neonatal period.

edges/14.description: Spinal involvement of the same dysplastic, osteopenic skeleton — compounded by lax spinal supporting tissue — produces progressive kyphoscoliosis.

edges/15.description: In the most severe (acceptor-subdomain p.Gly223Ser) genotypes the cranial sutures fuse prematurely, producing craniosynostosis with a prenatal Antley-Bixler-like appearance.

edges/16.description: Anterior chest wall deformity occurs as part of the generalized chondro-osseous dysplasia; a rib- or costal-cartilage-specific mechanism has not been dissected in this disorder.

edges/17.description: Broad, spatulate distal phalanges are grouped in the literature with the shared skeletal abnormalities of the linkeropathies; the digit-shaping mechanism itself is uncharacterized.

edges/18.description: Long, slender fingers accompany the radiographically long, thin tubular bones of the dysplasia; no digit-specific mechanism has been established.

edges/19.description: Mechanically weak periarticular capsule and ligament permit congenital and recurrent dislocation of the large joints.

edges/20.description: The same lax capsular and ligamentous tissue produces generalized joint hypermobility.

edges/21.description: Abnormal periarticular connective tissue also fixes joints, giving the characteristic coexistence of contractures with laxity.

edges/22.description: Talipes equinovarus (a fixed contracture-type deformity) and pes planovalgus (a laxity-type deformity) arise in the same abnormal periarticular connective tissue; the deformity-specific morphogenesis has not been studied in this disorder.

edges/24.description: Failed remodelling of the proteoglycan-dependent semilunar valve cushions yields a bicuspid aortic valve.

edges/25.description: Abnormal atrioventricular valve interstitial matrix manifests as mitral valve prolapse with variable regurgitation.

edges/26.description: Defective cardiac septation produces atrial and ventricular septal defects.

edges/27.description: A proteoglycan-deficient aortic media dilates from early infancy, producing progressive aortic root and ascending aortic dilatation.

evidence.snippet: We identified linkage to chromosome 11 and detected a mutation (c.830G>A, p.Arg277Gln) in B3GAT3, the gene coding for glucuronosyltransferase-I (GlcAT-I).
evidence.explanation: Original gene discovery establishing B3GAT3 as the cause of the Larsen-like joint dislocation plus congenital heart defect syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Independent in vitro assessment of each variant confirmed the B3GAT3: c.1A > G (p.Met1?) variant is functionally null and the c.671 T > A (p.L224Q) missense variant has significantly reduced glucuronyltransferase activity (~3% of control).
evidence.explanation: Functional confirmation that pathogenic B3GAT3 alleles act by loss of glucuronyltransferase activity, including a true null allele.

evidence.snippet: Clinical exome sequencing analysis revealed a homozygous c.416C>T variant in the B3GAT3 gene for the sister; the same variant was also present in the boy patient.
evidence.explanation: Documents a recurrent homozygous B3GAT3 allele in the Turkish population.

genes/0.notes: B3GAT3 (11q12.3) encodes beta-1,3-glucuronyltransferase 3 / glucuronosyltransferase-I (GlcAT-I), a cis- and cis-medial Golgi enzyme that transfers UDP-glucuronic acid onto the Gal-Gal-Xyl-Ser trisaccharide, completing the tetrasaccharide linker that all glycosaminoglycan chains are built upon. Reported disease alleles are predominantly missense substitutions in the glycosyltransferase catalytic domain (p.Arg277Gln — the original United Arab Emirates founder allele; p.Pro140Leu in the Nias/Indonesia clan; p.Gly223Ser in the severe craniosynostosis/fracture phenotype; p.Thr139Met recurrent in the Turkish population; p.Pro82Leu in a geroderma-like case; p.Arg161Trp and p.Arg297Trp in a compound heterozygote), together with a start-loss null allele (p.Met1?), a missense p.Leu224Gln with ~3% residual activity, and an in-frame p.Leu21del.

evidence.snippet: The boy underwent preoperative halo-gravity traction for severe kyphoscoliosis, followed by posterior instrumentation and fusion surgery without complications.
evidence.explanation: Documents the spinal surgical approach used and its uncomplicated outcome.

treatments/0.description: Management is entirely supportive; no disease-modifying therapy exists. Severe progressive kyphoscoliosis has been managed with preoperative halo-gravity traction followed by posterior instrumentation and spinal fusion. Joint dislocations, foot deformity and cervical instability are addressed by conventional orthopedic means, with the caveat that surgical results are often unsatisfactory in this connective tissue context.

evidence.snippet: DEXA confirmed severe osteopenia and delayed bone age despite bisphosphonates treatment; no fractures were reported.
evidence.explanation: Documents bisphosphonate use but with persistent severe osteopenia, so support for benefit is only partial.

treatments/1.description: Bisphosphonates have been used for the osteopenia/osteoporosis of B3GAT3 disease, but the reported outcomes are equivocal — one patient remained severely osteopenic with delayed bone age despite treatment. Evidence is anecdotal and no controlled data exist.

evidence.snippet: At the age of two, a heart ultrasound revealed an atrial septal defect, which was surgically treated three years later due to tachyarrhythmia and pulmonary hypertension.
evidence.explanation: Documents surgical repair of a septal defect prompted by complications.

treatments/2.description: Lifelong echocardiographic surveillance for valve disease and progressive aortic root/ascending aortic dilatation is warranted given the early onset reported (from two months of age), with surgical closure of haemodynamically significant septal defects. One reported patient required surgical ASD closure after developing tachyarrhythmia and pulmonary hypertension.

evidence.snippet: Both unaffected parents (double second cousins) were shown to be heterozygous carriers.
evidence.explanation: Confirms carrier status of consanguineous parents, the basis for recurrence-risk counseling.

treatments/3.description: Autosomal recessive inheritance implies a 25% recurrence risk for siblings. Counseling is particularly relevant given the high proportion of consanguineous families, the availability of recurrent founder alleles for targeted testing (p.Arg277Gln in the United Arab Emirates, p.Thr139Met in Turkey, p.Pro140Leu on Nias), and the prenatal detectability of the severe craniosynostosis/synostosis phenotype on ultrasound.

evidence.snippet: The heterogeneous LK phenotypes, ranging from mild to severe and even lethal presentations, seem to be related to specific B3GAT3 mutations, though there has been a limited number of patients and pathogenic variants described so far
evidence.explanation: States both the genotype-phenotype correlation and the small-sample caveat that keeps this hypothesis at EMERGING status.

hypotheses/0.description: Across the small published cohort, variants in the acceptor-substrate-binding subdomain of the GlcAT-I catalytic domain (p.Gly223Ser, p.Leu224Gln, p.Arg277Gln, p.Arg297Trp) segregate with the severe end of the spectrum — multiple fractures, craniosynostosis, cardiovascular malformation, and in the p.Gly223Ser cases death before one year — whereas donor-subdomain variants (p.Pro140Leu, p.Thr139Met, p.Arg161Trp) produce milder, sometimes purely skeletal disease. A compound heterozygote carrying one variant in each subdomain had an intermediate phenotype. The correlation rests on very few patients and is not yet supported by a systematic activity-versus-severity assay series, so it should be treated as emerging rather than as an established genotype-phenotype rule.

open_questions/0.rationale: The leading explanation for the cardiac specificity is that B3GAT3 is expressed more highly in heart than B3GALT6 and B4GALT7, so heart tissue is disproportionately sensitive to loss of this particular linker step. An alternative model holds that the linker enzymes act within a shared complex (a "GAGosome"), which would predict comparable rather than differential tissue sensitivity. Neither model has been tested directly in cardiac tissue, and the observation that the donor-subdomain p.Pro140Leu family had no cardiac phenotype at all suggests residual activity thresholds may matter as much as expression level.

open_questions/1.rationale: All five linker enzymes act sequentially on the same tetrasaccharide and produce overlapping phenotypes, yet the 2017 EDS nosology admits only B4GALT7 and B3GALT6 (as spEDS) and leaves B3GAT3, XYLT1 and XYLT2 outside. The comprehensive 2019 review argues these are a phenotypic continuum and proposes gene-prefixed "linkeropathy" naming. dismech currently follows MONDO and keeps this entry separate from Spondylodysplastic Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome; a linkeropathy Grouping would be the natural way to represent the union without collapsing the entities.

open_questions/2.rationale: Both systems block the same shared linker step, so a priori both GAG arms should fall together — and that is what human fibroblast measurements show. The zebrafish model instead shows CS virtually abolished with ~50% of HS retained, implying a species- or context-dependent prioritization of HS over CS when linker flux is limiting. This matters mechanistically: if the human disease also preferentially spares HS, then the skeletal/cartilage phenotype (CS-dependent pericellular matrix) should dominate over HS-dependent morphogen-signalling phenotypes, which is broadly what is observed clinically. The mismatch is unresolved because the human data are semi-quantitative and come from fibroblasts rather than cartilage or cardiac tissue.

open_questions/3.rationale: Midface hypoplasia and short/webbed neck are reported as particularly frequent in B3GAT3-related disorders, and hypertelorism recurs across reported patients, yet no study maps these features onto a specific craniofacial developmental process. The zebrafish b3gat3 mutant shows failed pericellular matrix formation in pharyngeal (craniofacial) cartilage, suggesting the facial skeleton's cartilage template is proteoglycan-dependent, but that observation has not been tied to the human facial gestalt, and hypertelorism and short neck could equally reflect cranial-base, suture, or cervical-vertebral mechanisms. No causal edge is asserted for these phenotypes pending mechanistic evidence.

open_questions/4.rationale: Hypotonia is described as ubiquitous and developmental delay as present in only some patients, but causation is unexamined: proteoglycans are co-receptors for morphogen signalling in neural development and B3GAT3 is expressed in skeletal muscle, yet no neuromuscular workup (EMG, muscle imaging or histology) or systematic neurodevelopmental study exists. Attribution is further confounded by single cases with cortical atrophy or perinatal cerebral infarction and by the motor limitation imposed by dislocations, contractures and fractures. No causal edge is asserted for these phenotypes pending such evidence.

open_questions/5.rationale: Both features rest on the same single severely affected p.Gly223Ser homozygous infant and have no mechanistic literature in this disorder. Plausible routes exist — glycosaminoglycans in the trabecular meshwork modulate aqueous outflow, and hearing loss could be conductive (ossicular or middle-ear connective tissue) or sensorineural — but neither the anatomic type of the hearing loss nor a glaucoma mechanism was characterized in the report. No causal edge is asserted for either phenotype; this records that decision as deliberate rather than an oversight.

open_questions/6.rationale: The Colman infant's corneal clouding and the Jones infant's lymphedema are clinical observations without a demonstrated corneal or lymphatic mechanism. Proteoglycan deficiency alone does not establish corneal deposition, endothelial injury, or lymphatic maldevelopment. These two phenotypes remain unconnected pending tissue-specific evidence; no frequency is inferred from single-case occurrence.

steps/2.description: Cytochrome P450-dependent bioactivation of a haloalkane hepatotoxicant generates a carbon-centred radical that binds covalently to hepatic macromolecules. The adduction is a measured quantity rather than an asserted step: covalent binding of 14C from labelled CCl4 is quantified against oxygen tension, added glutathione, cytochrome P-450 induction and CCl4 dose, and the protein-bound label localises to the cytochrome P-450 apoprotein mass range.

evidence.snippet: It can start with hepatocyte injury and advance to inflammation, which recruits and activates additional liver immune cells, leading to the activation of the hepatic stellate cells (HSCs).

steps/4.description: Hepatocyte death triggers activation of Kupffer cells and recruitment of inflammatory cells including macrophages.

steps/5.description: Activated Kupffer cells and recruited macrophages release profibrogenic cytokines and chemokines such as TGF-beta, IL-6, and TNF-alpha that activate hepatic stellate cells and perpetuate the fibrotic response.
