open_questions/0.rationale: The best whole-organism complex II model - an inducible systemic SDH-loss mouse - produces a lethal Leigh-like syndrome and validates the general consequence of complex II failure, and chronic hypoxia rescues it. However, it disrupts Sdhc, not SDHA, and uses abrupt complete knockout rather than the partial-function hypomorphic biallelic SDHA alleles that cause human disease. It therefore models complex II failure in general but not the SDHA genotype, residual-activity biology, or the human neuroanatomy of Leigh lesions. This is a translational-validity gap (a model exists but does not phenocopy the SDHA genotype/tissue context), so it is flagged as HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH. Isogenic CRISPR-corrected SDHA patient iPSC-derived neurons and organoids are the emerging route to a faithful model.

evidence.snippet: We performed homozygosity mapping and gene sequencing to identify the genetic defect in five complex I-deficient patients from three different families.

steps/1.description: Two damaged copies of NDUFAF3 (C3ORF60), which encodes a mitochondrial complex I assembly factor. The reported alleles span several mutation classes. The ClinGen expert-panel curation scored six variants across the first three reports: four missense changes, one initiation-codon change and one in-frame duplication. The leukoencephalopathy patient carries the in-frame duplication c.342_343insGTG p.117Valdup in trans with the missense c.505C>A p.Pro169Thr; the 2023 patient carries a splice-site variant in trans with a missense variant. No clean null allele has been reported.

evidence.snippet: NDUFAF3 co-immunoprecipitated with NDUFAF4, and three matrix arm structural subunits (NDUFS2, NDUFA9, NDUFS3) that are found in a 400 kDa assembly intermediate containing ND1.
evidence.explanation: What NDUFAF3 is physically part of, which is what this node is about, and the partner set that is lost with it.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, we show that NDUFAF3 tightly interacts with NDUFAF4 (C6ORF66), a protein previously implicated in complex I deficiency.
evidence.explanation: The NDUFAF3-NDUFAF4 association, which is why the NDUFAF4 disease (MC1DN15) and this one share an assembly lesion.

steps/2.description: NDUFAF3's place in complex I biogenesis is on the earliest assembly intermediates. It co-immunoprecipitates with NDUFAF4 and with the matrix-arm subunits NDUFS2, NDUFA9 and NDUFS3 in a roughly 400 kDa intermediate that also contains the mitochondrially encoded ND1 subunit. Losing it therefore removes a component from the step at which the nuclear-encoded matrix arm and the mtDNA-encoded membrane arm are first brought together.

evidence.snippet: Transient, short-term knock-down of the m-AAA protease AGF3L2 in cells that had been depleted of any of the early CI assembly factors completely rescued the ND1 labeling phenotype, confirming that it is not a synthesis defect, but rather results from rapid proteolysis of newly synthesized ND1.
evidence.explanation: The protease-knockdown rescue that identifies the mechanism as proteolysis, and names the protease responsible.

steps/3.description: ND1 is translated normally but destroyed shortly afterwards. Short-term knockdown of the m-AAA protease in cells depleted of NDUFAF3 completely restores ND1 labelling, which is what identifies the loss as proteolysis of an unprotected subunit rather than a failure to make it. The effect belongs to the early assembly factors specifically: knockdown of the late assembly factor NDUFAF2 does not produce it.

evidence.snippet: Two-dimensional, blue-native polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE) and sodium dodecyl sulfate-PAGE revealed reductions in Q-module (NDUFS2, NDUFS3, and NDUFA9) and P-module (NDUFB10 and NDUFB11) subunits, indicating disruption of mitochondrial complex I assembly.
evidence.explanation: The subunit-level description of the block in a patient, and the evidence that it spans both arms of the enzyme.

evidence.snippet: Accumulation of early sub-assemblies of the membrane arm of CI associated with mitochondrial complex I intermediate assembly (MCIA) complex was observed.
evidence.explanation: What accumulates behind the block, which is the complement of the subunit depletion and identifies the stage at which assembly stops.

evidence.snippet: The most striking additional findings were both the unusual occurrence of free monomeric CI holding MCIA and other assembly factors.
evidence.explanation: The second complexome finding in the same patient: the monomeric holoenzyme that does form has not released MCIA or the other assembly factors, which is a further sign that assembly does not run to completion.

steps/4.description: The holoenzyme does not complete. Two-dimensional blue-native and denaturing gels from the leukoencephalopathy patient show matrix-arm Q-module subunits (NDUFS2, NDUFS3, NDUFA9) and membrane-arm P-module subunits (NDUFB10, NDUFB11) reduced together, so the block is not confined to one module. Complexome profiling of the 2023 patient shows what piles up behind it: early membrane-arm sub-assemblies still bound to the MCIA complex. The same profiling reports a second, unusual species in that patient - free monomeric complex I still holding the MCIA complex and other assembly factors - so the holoenzyme that does form has not released its assembly machinery.

genes/0.notes:
NDUFAF3 (HGNC:29918, "NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase complex assembly factor 3") is at 3p21.31. Its previous symbol is C3orf60, which is the name under which the gene was described in 2009 and the name used in the older assembly literature; the HGNC record also lists the aliases MGC10527, DKFZP564J0123, E3-3 and 2P1.
The ClinGen Mitochondrial Disease Gene Curation Expert Panel classified the gene-disease relationship as Definitive on 7 March 2022 under SOP8, on case-level and experimental data from three publications plus model-organism support. Note what the assertion is against: ClinGen curated NDUFAF3 to "mitochondrial disease" (MONDO:0044970), not to MC1DN18, having deliberately lumped the NDUFAF3 phenotype into one disease entity. That is a different granularity decision from the one this entry makes, and it is recorded rather than resolved.

open_questions/0.rationale:
Prognosis is the question a family asks at diagnosis and the one this gene cannot currently answer. Most of the first seven reported patients died in infancy of severe neurological disease with lactic acidosis. Two later patients did not: a girl still alive at one year after a cavitating leukoencephalopathic crisis, and a child reported at ten with a neurodevelopmental disorder, dystonia and only a mild fibroblast complex I reduction. A 2025 series then added NDUFAF3 to the genes causing childhood-onset complex dystonia, which implies further survivors.
Two candidate explanations are available and neither has been tested. The first is residual function: every reported allele is missense, in-frame, splice-site or initiation-codon rather than a clean null, so different genotypes may leave different amounts of working assembly factor. The 2023 patient's biochemistry is consistent with that, in that the activity reduction is mild where the complexome defect is severe. The second is that fibroblast biochemistry simply does not track the neurological outcome, in which case the apparent correlation in that one patient is a coincidence and the assay is measuring the wrong tissue.
Distinguishing them matters clinically. If residual assembly-factor function predicts survival, a quantitative complexome measurement becomes a prognostic test at diagnosis. If it does not, it stays a diagnostic test only, and families should be counselled from the genotype and the clinical course rather than from the enzymology.

steps/12.description: Normal hematopoietic lineage choice is enforced by mutually antagonistic transcription factor networks (PU.1/SPI1 and CEBPA for myeloid, EBF1 and PAX5 for B, NOTCH1 and BCL11B for T). In MPAL these networks are disrupted or incompletely resolved, so no single program is consolidated and lineage-restricting feedback loops fail to close. The blast is left in a promiscuous, multi-lineage-primed transcriptional state.

evidence.snippet: We show that neither genetic profile nor transcriptome reliably correlate with specific MPAL immunophenotypes. Despite this, we find that MPAL blasts express a shared stem cell-like transcriptional profile indicative of high differentiation potential. Patients with the highest differentiation potential demonstrate inferior survival in our dataset.
evidence.explanation: Multiomic single-cell profiling of 14 newly diagnosed adult MPAL cases establishes the shared stem-like transcriptional state and links greater differentiation potential to worse survival.

evidence.snippet: Myeloid-B and myeloid-T MPAL show distinct mutation and methylation signatures that are associated with differences in lineage-commitment gene expressions.
evidence.explanation: Integrative genomic and methylation analysis ties the epigenetic state of MPAL directly to lineage-commitment gene expression.

evidence.snippet: Genome-wide methylation comparison among MPAL, AML, B-ALL, and T-ALL sub-classifies MPAL into AML-type and ALL-type MPAL, which is associated with better clinical response when lineage-matched therapy is given.
evidence.explanation: Shows the epigenetic lineage class is clinically actionable, supporting it as a real mechanistic layer rather than a descriptive one.

steps/13.description: Multiomic single-cell profiling shows that MPAL blasts, irrespective of their surface immunophenotype or driver genotype, converge on a shared stem-cell-like transcriptional program indicating high differentiation potential; the degree of that stemness tracks with survival. Genome-wide methylation separates MPAL into AML-like and ALL-like epigenetic classes whose lineage-commitment gene expression differs, so the epigenetic state, not only the mutation set, determines which lineage programs the blast can access. This node is the mechanistic bridge between a failed commitment decision and both the observed cross-lineage phenotype and the capacity for lineage switch.

steps/15.description: The defining, diagnostically operationalized event: blasts express lineage-assigning antigens of more than one lineage, either within a single population (biphenotypic) or as two coexisting populations (bilineal). WHO/ICC criteria assign myeloid lineage on myeloperoxidase expression or monocytic differentiation, T lineage on cytoplasmic or surface CD3, and B lineage on strong CD19 with at least one of CD79a, cytoplasmic CD22 or CD10, or weak CD19 with at least two of these. In acute undifferentiated leukemia the same machinery fails in the opposite direction and no lineage marker is expressed at all.

steps/16.description: Because alternative lineage programs remain transcriptionally accessible, MPAL clones can shift immunophenotype under therapeutic pressure. This is seen as spontaneous lymphoid-to-myeloid switching at relapse, and as antigen-loss or lineage-switch escape from lineage-directed immunotherapy such as CD19-targeted CAR T cells and blinatumomab. Plasticity is a major reason MPAL responds poorly to single-lineage-directed strategies and a principal driver of its inferior outcome relative to ALL.
